results.statement: sc-lint must give a consumer a method to override the interpreter that sc-lint runs sc_lint.* wheel helper steps on.
results.quote: Conflict question (team-lead, 2026-10-30): "GH-198.runner-argv against GH-198.kit-helpers. The literal rule \"a leading `python` becomes the `runner.python` interpreter\" would also rewrite `python -m sc_lint.*`. The kit-helpers record says those always use the kit interpreter, never overridden." Rand (2026-10-30): "a consumer must have a method to override behavior."
results.context: Phase M planning; Rand's ruling on a conflict question from team-lead, 2026-10-30 (lint-uwqw)
results.deterministic_check: A runner test with the consumer override set shows an sc_lint.lint_cargo_deny step resolves to the override interpreter.

relevant.instructions: Does item.text concern step argv construction, interpreter selection, runner.python, or sc_lint.* wheel helper execution in crates/sc-lint? Judge subject overlap only.

criteria.no: Silent about this obligation, explicitly denies an override.
criteria.unclear: Mentions helper interpreter behavior but leaves consumer override inclusion indeterminate.
criteria.yes: Specifically includes consumer-selectable helper interpreter override.

addressed.instructions: Does the item explicitly plan or preserve a consumer method to override the interpreter used for sc_lint.* wheel helper steps? Judge the specific obligation, separately from conflict or evidence. A kit default with an override qualifies.

criteria.unclear: The described behavior may or may not rule out consumer override.
criteria.yes: Explicitly forces a helper interpreter with no consumer override.

contradicted.instructions: Does item.text explicitly deny consumers any method to override the interpreter for sc_lint.* wheel helper steps? Judge conflict only. Omission, future deferral and unchanged unspecified behavior are not conflict; keeping a kit default while permitting overrides is compatible.
